locus.description: A fixed rear doorway in the cardiac gallery. A curved circumflex-shaped key connects the lateral room with the posterior septal room. This remains the same location on every review.

mnemonicSymbols.meaning: Posterior septal territory through the PDA

scenes.caption: The back-door key
scenes.transcript: At the rear door of the cardiac gallery, picture a curved circumflex key. Keep that same doorway as your memory location whenever coronary dominance returns.

scenes.caption: Dominance follows PDA origin
scenes.transcript: Coronary dominance follows the artery that gives rise to the posterior descending artery. On the angiogram, trace that vessel back to its parent artery.

scenes.caption: Left dominance: circumflex to PDA
scenes.transcript: In a left-dominant circulation, the posterior descending artery comes from the circumflex. Its septal branches supply the posterior part of the interventricular septum.

scenes.caption: Lateral wall plus posterior septum
scenes.transcript: The circumflex also supplies the lateral left ventricular wall through its branches. A clot at its origin can therefore threaten both territories downstream.

scenes.caption: Combine the two territories
scenes.transcript: For the book's example, combine the lateral left ventricular wall with the posterior septum. Identifying only one of those regions would leave out part of the pattern.

scenes.caption: Retrieve the territory
scenes.transcript: Return to the rear door: the circumflex key opens the lateral room and the back septal room. The recall cue is simple: left dominance, circumflex supplies the back.

realImages.title: Coronary angiograms showing right and left dominance
realImages.caption: Real coronary angiograms: panel (a) shows a right-sided origin of the posterior descending artery; panel (b) illustrates left coronary dominance. Red arrows identify the posterior descending artery in the published figure.
realImages.displayNotes: For the left-dominance lesson, direct attention to panel (b), the right half of the figure. Keep source panel labels and attribution visible or accessible. This figure illustrates dominance, not the particular occlusion described in the source MCQ.

quiz.prompt: In left-dominant coronary circulation, an occlusion at the origin of the circumflex artery most directly threatens which combined territory?
options: Anterior left ventricular wall and anterior septum
Lateral left ventricular wall and posterior septum
quiz.explanation: In left dominance, the circumflex gives rise to the posterior descending artery. A proximal circumflex occlusion therefore threatens its lateral-wall branches and the PDA territory, including the posterior septum.

title: Extralobar Sequestration: Its Own Pleural Coat

locus.description: A fixed coat hook beside the entrance to the thoracic gallery holds a small lung parcel in its own coat. Keep the hook and coat in this same location on every review.

mnemonicSymbols.meaning: Extralobar tissue outside the main lung covering

scenes.caption: Extra means an extra coat
scenes.transcript: At the coat hook in the thoracic gallery, imagine an extra lung parcel wearing its own coat. Keep this same hook as the permanent location for extralobar sequestration.

scenes.caption: Systemic arterial supply
scenes.transcript: Pulmonary sequestration is abnormal lung tissue without the usual connection to the tracheobronchial tree. It receives arterial blood from the systemic circulation, commonly through an aortic branch.

scenes.caption: Its own visceral pleura
scenes.transcript: Extralobar means the sequestered tissue has a separate visceral pleural covering. In the operative photograph, focus on the distinct pleural envelope around the lesion.

scenes.caption: The pleural relationship
scenes.transcript: An intralobar sequestration instead lies within the surrounding lung and shares its pleural covering. The difference tested here is the relationship to visceral pleura.

scenes.caption: Read the covering
scenes.transcript: Use the relationship to pleura to identify the extralobar form, and keep the feeding vessel as a separate anatomical feature. This distinction makes the question much easier.

scenes.caption: Retrieve the extra coat
scenes.transcript: Return to the coat hook and say: extra means an extra coat. In this lesson, that coat represents its own visceral pleura. Retrieve the feature before choosing an answer.

realImages.title: Extralobar pulmonary sequestration at thoracoscopy
realImages.caption: Real thoracoscopic views of an extralobar pulmonary sequestration. Panel A shows the separate lesion covered by its own pleura. Panel D depicts an associated bronchogenic cyst, not the sequestration.
realImages.displayNotes: Focus the lesson on panel A. Panels B and C show the stalk; panel D shows a different associated lesion. Do not highlight all four panels as if each represents the tested pleural feature.
realImages.author: Carolyn Hanna; Priya G. Sharma; Moiz M. Mustafa; Jennifer Reppucci; Archana Shenoy; Dhanashree Rajderkar
realImages.attribution: Hanna et al., Figure 4, Egyptian Journal of Radiology and Nuclear Medicine 52:54 (2021), doi:10.1186/s43055-021-00440-1. CC BY 4.0. Unmodified.

focusRegion.label: Panel A: sequestration with its own pleural covering

quiz.prompt: A sequestered lung segment receives systemic arterial blood. Which finding identifies the extralobar form?
options: Normal pulmonary arterial branching through the hilum
A normal connection to a segmental bronchus
A shared visceral pleural covering with adjacent lung
Its own separate visceral pleural covering
quiz.explanation: Extralobar sequestration has its own visceral pleural envelope, separate from the adjacent lung. Systemic arterial supply is a feature of sequestration and alone does not distinguish extralobar from intralobar disease.

locus.description: A fixed pair of double doors at the vascular gallery has four number locks above the frame. The widening door cues diameter; four locks cue the fourth power. Keep this position stable in future reviews.

scenes.caption: Four locks: fourth power
scenes.transcript: At the double doors of the vascular gallery, imagine four number locks above the frame. Widening the doorway changes resistance through a fourth-power relationship.

scenes.caption: Resistance follows one over radius to the fourth
scenes.transcript: For steady laminar flow in the ideal tube model, resistance is proportional to viscosity and length, and inversely proportional to the fourth power of radius.

scenes.caption: Two to the fourth is sixteen
scenes.transcript: If diameter doubles, radius doubles too. Raise that factor of two to the fourth power: two times two times two times two equals sixteen.

scenes.caption: Sixteen divided by sixteen equals one
scenes.transcript: Resistance therefore becomes one sixteenth of its original value when length and viscosity stay unchanged. Starting from sixteen resistance units, the new value is one unit.

scenes.caption: Use the model assumptions
scenes.transcript: This is an idealized laminar-flow relationship. In real circulation, pulsation, branching, and vessel compliance affect how pressure and flow behave. Keep the model assumptions in mind.

scenes.caption: Retrieve the fourth-power rule
scenes.transcript: Return to the double doors and the four locks. Remember: double diameter, divide resistance by sixteen. The answer to this example is one peripheral resistance unit.

realImages.title: Human artery in cross section
realImages.caption: A real bright-field micrograph of a human artery. The central lumen provides anatomical context for the lesson on vessel radius and resistance.
realImages.displayNotes: This is a real anatomical example, not a measurement of the numerical scenario. Do not claim that the image demonstrates a doubled diameter or a measured sixteenfold resistance change. The calculation applies to the lesson's stated idealized assumptions.

realImages.attribution: Human artery photomicrograph by Lord of Konrad; Commons color adjustment by Tilifa Ocaufa. Wikimedia Commons, Artery.png. CC0 1.0.

quiz.prompt: Under Poiseuille's model, vessel length and viscosity remain unchanged. Resistance is initially 16 PRU. If diameter doubles, what is the new resistance?
quiz.explanation: Doubling diameter also doubles radius. Resistance changes by 1 / 2^4 = 1/16 when the other model variables stay fixed. Therefore 16 PRU becomes 1 PRU.
